verdict: Lend selectively in Bhimavaram aquaculture — pursue feed-linked and diagnostic-backed shrimp farmers with tight monthly structure; avoid disease-exposed single-pond operators and export-only processors until pond-level data is collected.
title: Bhimavaram Fisheries & Aquaculture: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Bhimavaram sits in West Godavari, a brackishwater shrimp cluster where cash is made in ponds, not in offices.** A farmer buys seed, feed and power, grows shrimp over a cycle, and sells to a processor or exporter who pays after grading and shipment. Feed is the largest cash cost and is bought on short credit; the farmer's real risk is a single disease event wiping the pond. **So when a proposal lands, check the pond count, stocking density and whether the borrower owns or leases the land; if leased, ask for the lease term against the loan tenor.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits with whoever controls feed supply and export grading, not with the pond.** Peer results show the spread: Sharat Industries grew revenue 37.89% YoY to Rs 524.72 crore for FY26 [5], while Avanti's feed realisation is being tested against sticky fishmeal costs [7]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower is a farmer, a feed dealer or a processor; if a processor, ask for the export order book and buyer concentration.**

## What has changed now
**The local support infrastructure is improving.** A state-of-the-art aquaculture diagnostic laboratory was inaugurated at Bhimavaram under a KCT–ICAR-CIBA partnership, with soil and water health cards and the Vanami Shrimpapp for diagnostic results [1]. Separately, AP is developing an integrated aqua corridor linking six fisheries centres [2]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower uses diagnostic services; if not, ask why, and price the disease risk accordingly.** Note the corridor source is a single local report [2] and the lab is new [1] — neither yet shows up in borrower cash flows.

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue feed dealers with diversified farmer bases, diagnostic-adopting farmers with multiple ponds, and processors with confirmed export orders.** Avoid single-pond borrowers and those with no disease history. **Take a monthly pond-wise stocking and mortality statement, feed purchase invoices, and a post-harvest sale reconciliation; if mortality crosses the borrower's own stated threshold, ask for a stock visit before the next disbursement.** Structure as short-tenor cycle loans with a moratorium matched to harvest, not annual working capital.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch feed credit rollover, delayed harvest, and buyer rejection notes.** Rating commentary flags that clustered shrimp farming multiplies disease and can wipe out almost 90% of a pond's population [9]. **If a borrower's feed dealer reports stretched credit or a skipped cycle, ask for the pond inspection report and freeze fresh limits.**
watch: Mortality above borrower's stated threshold -> stock visit before next disbursement
Feed purchase invoices vs sales reconciliation (monthly)
Feed credit rollover beyond one cycle -> freeze fresh limits, ask for pond inspection
Buyer rejection or order cancellation -> reprice or reduce limit
Diagnostic lab usage and soil/water health card (quarterly)
No diagnostic use for two cycles -> treat as higher disease risk, tighten structure
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: New Bhimavaram diagnostic lab and AP aqua corridor plan improve local support infrastructure.
